info.name: FirstChekout API Gateway
info.description:
Introduction

FirstChekout API Gateway provides a secure and reliable way for merchants to accept and manage payments across multiple channels.

With this API, you can:

  • Initiate and track transactions

  • Accept payments via cards, bank transfer, USSD, and more

  • Manage payment flows programmatically

  • Ensure secure authentication and data handling

This documentation will guide you through the steps required to integrate and start processing payments successfully.

Payment API Integration Guide

This guide explains how to successfully complete a payment using the API.

🌐 Environment Configuration

Before making API requests, ensure you are using the correct environment URLs.

Sandbox Environment

Use the following base URLs for testing:

Variable URL
gatewayUrl https://www.firstchekoutdev.com/apigateway
identityUrl https://www.firstchekoutdev.com/identityserver
iisIdentityUrl https://www.firstchekoutdev.com/identityserver

Production / LIVE Environment

Use the following base URLs for live transactions:

Variable URL
gatewayUrl https://www.firstchekout.com/apigateway
identityUrl https://www.firstchekout.com/identityserver
iisIdentityUrl https://www.firstchekout.com/identityserver

Prerequisites (Required Credentials)

Before you begin, log in to your Merchant Dashboard and retrieve the following credentials:

  • merchantId

  • clientId

  • clientSecret

  • clientEncryptionKey

  • publicKey

  • secretKey

📌 Important:

  • Keep these credentials secure and private

  • A guide to how to retrieve these can be found here.

  • Do not expose them in frontend applications or public repositories

  • They are required for authentication, encryption, and request signing

Overview

To process a payment, follow these steps:

  1. Generate Access Token

  2. Initiate Transaction

  3. Make Payment using the options (USSD, CARD, QR, PAYATTITUDE, FirstEase and Pay With Transfer)

  4. Refresh Token (if expired)

  5. Query Transaction to see the details of a transaction using it's unique transactionReference (optional)

1️⃣ Generate Access Token

Before making any API call, you must authenticate.

  • Call the Generate Access Token endpoint

  • You will receive an access token

  • The token is valid for 600 seconds (10 minutes)

🔑 Important:
Include this token in the header of all subsequent requests.

2️⃣ Initiate Transaction

Create a new transaction for the payment.

  • Call the Initiate Transaction endpoint

  • You will receive a transactionReference, which you can store in transactionReference to re-use within this collection.

Example:

TX-A43C8A1036204BD392D6438A6CAEF0AE

Note:
This transactionReference uniquely identifies the transaction and will be used in the next steps.

3️⃣ Make Payment

Once the transaction reference is generated, proceed with payment.

Available payment methods include:

  • Card

  • Bank Transfer

  • USSD

  • FirstEase

  • PayAttitude

  • QR

Note: Use the same transactionReference when making the payment.

Transactions are only valid for a limited period of time. If the transaction expires, subsequent payment attempts may return errors such as:

  • Transaction Expired

  • Transaction Not Found

When this happens, you must restart the transaction flow by:

  1. Calling the Initiate Transaction endpoint again to generate a new transactionReference

  2. Proceeding with payment using the newly generated transaction reference

Query Transaction (optional)

Retrieve the details of a specific transaction using its unique reference.

  • Call the Query Transaction endpoint

  • Pass the transactionReference

✅ Successful Response:

  • Status = "OK"

  • Transaction details are returned

🔄 Token Expiry

  • The access token expires after 600 seconds

  • If any request fails due to expiration:

Generate a new token and retry the request

Summary

1. Generate Token
2. Initiate Transaction
3. Make Payment
4. Refresh Token (if needed)
5. Query Transaction (if needed)

Best Practices

  • Always check transaction status before payment

  • Store the transactionReference securely

  • Handle token expiration gracefully

  • Log API responses for debugging

request.description:
Payment Status

The status field represents the current state of a transaction.

Possible values are:

  • SUCCESS — Payment was completed successfully.

  • PENDING — Payment has been initiated but is still being processed.

  • FAILED — Payment was not successful.

  • NOT_COMPLETED — Payment process was started but not completed by the customer.

  • INITIATED — Transaction has been created but payment has not yet been completed.

Process secure card payments with encrypted card data and OTP verification. All card data must be encrypted using AES-256 before transmission to ensure PCI DSS compliance. You can copy ready-to-use JavaScript and C# encryption blocks directly from this guide.

Click on the link and scroll to the AES Encryption Implementation section to view the code.
